instruction: Sort the WeeklySales data by the Sales column in descending order, so the highest Sales week appears first.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully created a clustered column chart on Sheet2 with title 'Sales & COGS' showing Sales and COGS data for 10 weeks in LibreOffice Calc.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Calc, create new sheets, insert and configure charts, set chart titles and types, select data ranges
metadata.task_rationale: Tests data sorting skills in the same spreadsheet context. Different operation (sort vs chart) but same complexity level.
metadata.explanation: Task requires sorting data by Sales column descending. Getter reads week labels and sales values from rows 2-11. Metric checks descending order (0.5) and exact value positions (0.5).

scoring_breakdown.descending_order: 0.5 - Sales values are in descending order
scoring_breakdown.correct_positions: 0.5 - Each value matches expected sorted position (0.05 each)

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads Sales column (column 2) from rows 2-11, skipping header row, which properly extracts the sorted state needed for verification.
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' - directly accesses expected.get('expected_sales_order') without wrapping in rules/type lookup.
Two-part scoring (0.5 descending order + 0.5 exact position match) provides good coverage: checks both the general sorting property and specific value positions.
Postconfig properly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring the sorted state is persisted to disk.
Expected values are in proper descending order and appear plausible for a WeeklySales dataset.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The getter hardcodes column 2 as the Sales column. If the spreadsheet has additional columns before Sales, this would read wrong data. Consider adding a header-row scan to dynamically locate the 'Sales' column.

Minor: Expected values cannot be independently verified without access to the actual xlsx file. If the values don't match the real data, the exact-position check (0.5 weight) would incorrectly penalize a correct sort.
